answer: An honest AI agent must invest 1 unit of verified labor to complete a task, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units to achieve parity, ensuring that operational costs remain non-amortizable for the attacker. The verifier monitors a ferrous task stream to block replay, scanning each jetty of the state transition graph for duplicate work. If an audit detects a fraud-proof mismatch or replayed output, it uses the evidence as an anchor for identity revocation. The protocol assumes tasks are atomic and non-shareable, casting a lantern of transparency upon every transition to prevent parallel fake.
